title.narrative: Svenska Röda Korset- Katastrofriskreducering och klimatanpassningsarbete i Sudan
Swedish Red Cross- Disaster Risk Reduction and Climate Change Adaption in Sudan

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the project was to contribute to strengthened resilience of women, girls, men and boys in targeted high-risk vulnerable communities in Sudan, through the reduction of disaster risks including adaptation to climate change.
The specific objective of the project was to strengthen the technical capacities of SRCS within Protection Gender Inclusion (PGI), Community Engagement Accountability (CEA), sensitive Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Climate Change Adaption (CCA), and community resilience.

Projektet kommer att genomföras i samarbete mellan Svenska Röda Korset (SRC) och Sudanesiska Röda Halvmånen (SRCS). Det föreslagna projektet är nytt för den svenska ambassaden i Khartoum. Sida/Ambassadens fond kommer att stödja 10 samhällen och upprätthålla ett visst stöd till 12 samhällen, som tidigare stöddes av SRC och Radiohjalpen mellan (2018-2021). Stödet till de 12 samhällena kommer att vara i mindre utsträckning för att fånga upp lärande och se till att SRCS lokala volontärnätverk kan fortsätta att stödja samhällena. Det föreslagna projektet kommer att genomföras i fyra stater i Röda havet, Norra Kordofan, Nilen och norra stater, med inriktning på cirka 146 000 individer i 22 samhällen (cirka 51% kvinnor och 49% män) och 240 av SRCS personal och volontärer på nationell, filial och samhällsnivå (cirka 60% kvinnor och 40% män). De berörda staterna är känsliga för översvämningar, extrem temperatur, ökenspridning, torka och sanddrift. Samhällena själva är i störst behov av kapacitetsutveckling för att bedöma, hantera och minska katastrofrisker och anpassa sig till klimatförändringarnas effekter. Dessutom har SRCS i de fyra riktade staterna goda strukturer inklusive en stark volontärbas.
Syftet med det föreslagna projektet är att öka samhällenas medvetenhet om risker och faror och hur de kan förebyggas samt att stärka samhällenas kunskap om sina risker. Projektet kommer att installera samhällsbaserade system för tidig varning och katastrofinsatsgrupper. Projektet kommer att utföra olika typer av medvetandehöjande aktiviteter, t.ex. riskkartläggning, säkra områden och utrymningsvägar. etc. Resultaten av projektet kommer att bidra till att förbättra levnadsvillkoren för de berörda samhällena. De långsiktiga effekterna är relaterade till institutionella och beteendemässiga förändringar. Genom den förstärkta beredskapen för katastrofer kommer människors motståndskraft att stärkas och deras sårbarhet för faror att minska. Detta kommer på lång sikt att ha en positiv inverkan på stabilitet, säkerhet, konfliktlösning och fredlig utveckling.

The project will be implemented in partnership between Swedish Red Cross (SRC) and Sudanese Red Crescent Society (SRCS). The proposed project is new to the Swedish Embassy in Khartoum. Sida/Embassy's fund will support 10 communities and maintain some support to 12 communities, which earlier supported by SRC and Radiohjalpen between (2018-2021). The support to the 12 communities will be to lesser extent, to capture learning and ensure that the SRCS local volunteer network is capable to continue supporting the communities. The proposed project will be implemented in four states in Red Sea, North Kordofan, River Nile and Northern states, targeting approximately 146,000 individuals in 22 communities (approximately 51% women and 49% men) and 240 of SRCS staff and volunteers at national, branch and community level (approximately 60% women and 40% men). The targeted states are sensitive to flooding, extreme temperature, desertification, drought and sand drifts. The communities themselves are in greatest need for capacity development in assessing, managing and reducing disaster risks and adapting to climate change impacts. In addition, SRCS in the four targeted states have good structures including a strong volunteer base.
The aim of proposed project to increase communities' awareness of risks and hazards and how to prevent them, and to strengthen communities' knowledge of their risks. The project will install community based early warning system and disaster response teams. The project will perform different kinds of awareness raising activities e.g. risk mapping exercise, safe areas and evacuation routes. etc. The results of the project will contribute to improve the living conditions of the targeted communities. The longer term effects are related to institutional and behavioural change. Through the enhanced preparedness to disasters, people’s resilience will be strengthened and their vulnerabilities to hazards decreased. This will in the long-term have a positive impact on stability, security, conflict resolution and peaceful development.

The DRRCCA project contributed to improved resilience across 16 communities in Northern, River Nile and Red Sea states. Overall, the project increased the capacity of women, girls, men, and boys, in the targeted communities to cope with, mitigate, prepare for and respond to disasters and climate change. According to baseline and endline surveys, the percentage of women, men, girls and boys who can identify at least 3 preparedness and response measures substantially increased from 4% to 61%. The percentage of women, men, girls and boys who can identify at least 3 mitigation measures related to disaster risk reductions, climate change and natural hazards significantly increased from 3% to 50%.
According to the projects theory of change and final report, Protection, Gender and Inclusion and Community Engagement and Accountability (PGI/CEA) mainstreaming placed the needs and capacities of all targeted people at the centre of the project design and delivery. From the start of the project, decisions and actions were taken to ensure that the basics of PGI mainstreaming were included in all trainings. By the end of the project, there was clear evidence that PGI mainstreaming was taken into consideration at every step, so that community activities were striving to be more inclusive.
SRCS staff and volunteer capacities in environmental sustainability were strengthened, contributing towards environmental sustainability mainstreaming in the community actions plans and in the project small-scale mitigation activities.
The project strengthened the capacity of SRCS governance, staff and volunteers in community-based DRR, CCA and resilience. SRCS governance, project related staff and volunteers were trained in these topics, as well as advocated to relevant stakeholders, such as religious leaders, community leaders, and other NGOs, for better mitigation, preparedness and response in communities. All targeted branches reported an improved score in their DRRCCA technical capacity self-assessment.
Result examples under each outcome area (outcome and output):
Outcome 1: SRCS governance, staff and volunteers have DRR and CCA technical capacity to deliver and support community - based DRR and CCA programming
- 82% of SRCS governance, project related staff and volunteers were trained in DRR, CCA and resilience (baseline 30%, target 75%).
- 100% of the targeted branches had an improved score in their DRR/CCA technical capacity self-assessment (baseline 0%, target 100%).
- Practical tools were developed and made available for SRCS staff and volunteers to implement quality PGI/CEA sensitive DRR/CCA/resilience activities: awareness materials for 1) natural hazards, climate change risks and mitigation measures and 2) preparedness and response were standardized and contextualized. One set of practical tools was developed. Tools were piloted in two communities, and after feedback from communities utilised in all 8 targeted communities.
Outcome 2: SRCS governance, staff and volunteers have the technical capacity at programme and institutional level to mainstream Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI), Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA) and environmental sustainability
- 78% of SRCS governance, project related staff and volunteers in the targeted branches participated in PGI/CEA mainstreaming training (target 75%).
- All targeted branches improved their PGI capacity from 60% at baseline to 100% by endline (target 100%).
- 68% of SRCS governance, project related staff and volunteers in the targeted branches participated in environmental sustainability training (baseline 0%, target 75%).
- 100% of community action plans had environmental considerations (baseline 0%, target 100%).
- 100% of the small-scale mitigation activities considered environmental sustainability (baseline 0%, target 100%).
- The development of SRCS's institutional capacity within PGI/CEA and environmental sustainability led to strengthened capacities of the targeted communities in these areas. For example, in all targeted localities and communities, each Community Disaster Response Team (CDRT) and each Early Warning System (EWS) committee includes a designated PGI focal person responsible for considering the different impacts of hazards on women, girls, men and boy during the planning and implementation of actions (c.f. below).
Outcome 3: Increased capacity of women, girls, men and boys, in the targeted communities to cope with, mitigate, prepare for and respond to disasters and climate change
Outcome 3 delivered clear on-the-ground results.
- All targeted communities completed Enhanced Vulnerability and Capacity Assessments (EVCA), including risk mapping. 532 women, girls, men and boys took part in the EVCA. The community participants identified hazards and risks during the EVCA process. Based on the EVCA findings, small-scale mitigation activities were included in community action plans and conducted in the communities.
- 100% of targeted communities implemented small-scale mitigation measures (baseline 0%, target 100%). The project covered one or two activities per community, depending on their priorities and the available budget. Implemented community activities were for example: the creation of water harvesting terraces, flooding terraces, rehabilitation of wells, palm leaves distribution, river bank stabilisation, fire control and the establishment of home gardens.
The activities/measures improved communities' resilience to disaster risks and supported income and livelihoods. Interventions continue after the project end, for example the provision of electricity through local community initiatives and the creation of committees to oversee the infrastructure and ensure sustainability. All activities were collaborative efforts involving community members, volunteers and SRCS, and when needed technical expertise.
- The percentage of women, men, girls and boys who can identify at least 3 mitigation measures related to disaster risk reductions, climate change and natural hazards significantly increased from 3% to 50% (target 65%).
- The percentage of women, men, girls and boys who can identify at least 3 preparedness and response measures substantially increased from 4% to 61% (target 65%).
- 100% of targeted communities developed contingency plans (baseline 0%, target 100%) and 8 CDRTs were trained in DRR and using tools and equipment (baseline 0, target 8) to prepare for and provide effective response to disasters.
- Six locality-level Early Warning System (EWS) Committees were formulated in Northern, Red Sea and River Nile with 64 members. 60 EWS committee members, women and men, were trained (target 60). The project conducted an early simulation exercise involving 1 452 participants, community members and responsible stakeholders. Communities provided feedback. Concrete community-specific evacuation and response plans were developed. The exercise enhanced preparedness and response capacity. As a result, 87% of women, girls, men and boys reported that they are satisfied with the EWS (baseline 37%, target 70%).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
